statement: Ford-Fulkerson on a network with integer capacities terminates after at most m augmenting-path iterations (m = number of edges), no matter which augmenting paths are chosen.
definitions: Ford-Fulkerson = the generic augmenting-path method: repeatedly pick ANY s-t path with positive residual capacity in the current residual network (including reverse arcs created by earlier augmentations) and augment by its bottleneck; one iteration = one augmentation. Capacities are positive integers; the claim quantifies over all valid choices of paths.
